text:
Shea Theodore is doing the hard part for Vegas. He plays 22:15 a night, the Golden Knights get almost 58% of the 5-on-5 chance quality with him on the ice, and that share is nearly 8 points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey saw the same thing last season: with teammates, opponents and zone starts accounted for, his team created 0.13 more expected goals per 60 with him out there, 87th percentile among defensemen.

The scoresheet tells a thinner story. He has 8 points in 26 games, no goals in his last ten, and our wins-added measure (how much a player's goals swung win chances) ranks him 549th of 567 skaters. Some of that is luck: Vegas has scored 4.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that gap usually closes. He's also doing quieter work, with 41 blocked shots. The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted him sliding in to stack the pads on a McDavid rebound in Edmonton. Our numbers project about 35 points.
headline: Shea Theodore drives play; the points haven't followed
